prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry holds thresholds, connection/gate/towing/stand rules, border states, preference visibility, CTT tolerance, swap precedence/equity/customs eligibility/min notification/prohibited trades. Modes (ADM=Airport Duty Manager declares): Normal(en-route alerts only); Adverse Weather(sweep intervals may shorten); Capacity Reduction State(binding metering; localized for apron contamination/stand closures); Recovery Phase(RFM exits); Contingency Fallback(Contingency Operations Console); Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms). Recovery preserves operator commercial logic. Actors: RFM=Regional Flow Manager; Airspace Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison; Tower Supervisor(stand readiness not movement clearance); ADM(Medical Diversion Notice, Customs Hold Release Note); Ramp Control Lead(sweep areas; Apron Sweep Completion Note); Ground Handling Dispatcher(Towbar Shortage Report; sweep staff; updates Handling Resource Planner); Aircraft Operator Rep(Crew Duty Extension Log; identifies swap flights); Airline Operations Coordinator(revised TOBT incl. cleaning delays; enters swap: flight IDs, reason, readiness basis, effective time); Slot Coordinator; NOL=Network Operations Liaison; Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator; MBO=Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward. Parts: Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform; Airline Interface Adapter; Sector Load Monitor; Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service; CAM=Capacity Assessment Module(AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate; Arrival Regulation Console; Tactical Regulation Proposal); Weather Ingest Gateway; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time, retained until delay exceeds tolerance; GDP=Ground Delay Program; Pushback Window Token; evaluates swaps vs GDP/CTT/TOBT/AAR); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(TOBT=Target Off Block Time; Collaborative Decision Log; stand readiness records; validates users via Identity Access Service, blocks non-delegated); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager; suppresses release if stand not ready/route blocked); Gate Conflict Detector(readiness vs allocation/towing/adjacent stands); Audit Event Ledger(readiness, acknowledgements, hazard closures, releases); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Alert Distribution Hub; Common Situation Display. Rules: sweep confirmation valid through pushback; expiry→inspection-required, recheck.

New part:
S671: The Slot Coordinator reviews any exception raised by the Slot Allocation Engine and confirms whether the swap remains consistent with regional flow objectives.
S672: Slot Coordinator sends the Slot Swap Permission Email only after the governance checks have been completed and recorded.
S673: For airline-to-airline coordination, each Aircraft Operator Representative records concurrence in the Airport CDM Portal rather than relying on a verbal agreement.
S674: The Network Operations Liaison monitors aggregate displacement from approved substitutions to ensure that one carrier's recovery action does not destabilize the wider network plan.
S675: The Regional Flow Manager may suspend collaborative substitution during a Capacity Reduction State when scarce capacity must be protected for the published tactical plan.
S676: The Tower Supervisor retains authority to reject a swap if the resulting sequence would conflict with safe runway sequencing or local control workload.
S677: The Ramp Control Lead confirms that the revised sequence remains compatible with stand occupancy, pushback spacing, and tug availability shown on the Ramp Movement Board.
S678: Airport Duty Manager uses the Apron Sweep Completion Note to confirm that apron availability constraints do not invalidate an approved substitution.
S679: Airline Operations Coordinator uses the release note to confirm that a candidate substitution is eligible for customs release before requesting a slot swap.
S680: Customs release status is treated as a prerequisite condition for any substitution that would move an international departure into an earlier operating position.
S681: If customs status is incomplete, the Airport CDM Portal keeps the proposal pending and prevents the Slot Allocation Engine from publishing the revised slot assignment.
S682: The Collaborative Decision Log captures the proposed flights, the reason code, the user confirmations, the governance outcome, and the final decision time.
S683: The Audit Event Ledger records each approval, rejection, cancellation, and override so that later review can distinguish operational judgment from system enforcement.
S684: The Flight Data Exchange publishes revised Flight Intent Message content only after the approved substitution is final and time synchronized.
S685: The Common Situation Display presents the updated Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time so that operational users share the same view of the accepted change.
S686: The Departure Metering Service recalculates metering advisories after approval and prevents the swap from creating a new demand peak at a departure fix.
S687: Disputes between operators are escalated to the Regional Flow Manager when the recorded concurrences conflict or when a party alleges that governance rules were bypassed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
